descripcion: At C2 disagreement is precise about which part of a claim is contested — the premise, the logic, or the conclusion — rather than a blanket reaction. This precision is what separates expert disagreement from ordinary pushback.

filas: I'd question the starting assumption there.
I don't think that conclusion actually follows.
I'll grant the reasoning, but not where it ends up.

ejemplos.texto: I'd question the starting assumption there, before we even get to the argument.
I don't think that conclusion actually follows from the evidence given.
I'll grant the reasoning, but I don't think it ends up where you think it does.

notas: Naming the level of disagreement (premise, logic, conclusion) shows the other person exactly where to focus a response, rather than forcing them to guess.
I'll grant… but… concedes something specific before disagreeing, which is more persuasive than a flat no.
This precision matters most in genuinely technical or academic disagreement, where a vague no wastes everyone's time.

contraste.es: Spanish has the same building blocks (no comparto la premisa – I don't accept the premise; concedo que – I grant that; de ahí no se sigue – it doesn't follow), so precise disagreement transfers almost word for word.
contraste.de: German has the same building blocks (ich teile die Prämisse nicht; zugegeben – granted; daraus folgt nicht – it doesn't follow). Note that I grant that is more neutral than ich gebe zu, which suggests a reluctant admission.
contraste.it: Italian has the same building blocks (non condivido la premessa; concedo che – I grant that; non ne consegue – it doesn't follow), so precise disagreement transfers almost word for word.
contraste.fr: French has a particularly close match in je vous accorde que (I grant you that), and il ne s'ensuit pas que corresponds to it doesn't follow that. Precise disagreement therefore transfers almost word for word.
contraste.pt: Portuguese has the same building blocks (não partilho a premissa; concedo que – I grant that; daí não decorre – it doesn't follow), so precise disagreement transfers almost word for word.

errores: Disagreeing globally when the actual objection is only to one specific level.
Using it doesn't follow as a vague dismissal rather than a precise logical objection.
Failing to grant anything, which makes the disagreement sound total rather than targeted.

autochequeo: Have I identified exactly which level (premise, logic, conclusion) I'm disagreeing with?
Have I granted anything specific before disagreeing?
Would the other person know precisely where to focus a response?
Have I avoided a vague, global disagreement where a targeted one would serve better?
Would an expert in this field find the objection precise, not vague?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the precision of the disagreement. Check whether the level of disagreement (premise, logic, conclusion) is named clearly. Do not rewrite the text.
